Consult Summary:
- 33-year-old female nurse with 7-day history of fever, night sweats, myalgias and nausea following travel to Vietnam 4 weeks ago; malaria to be excluded.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Fever for approximately 7 days with intermittent hot and cold episodes, profuse sweating (including nocturnal sweating), generalized muscle aches, nausea with reduced oral intake, fatigue and malaise.
- Associated symptoms / systems review:
  - No cough, no sore throat, no ear pain, no diarrhea, no neck stiffness.
  - Headache: baseline chronic headaches related to screen use; no new severe headache or migraine currently.
  - No rash noted, no swollen/tender peripheral joints.
  - No urinary symptoms (no dysuria, no frequency).
- Pertinent negatives:
  - Denies respiratory, gastrointestinal (diarrhea), ENT, urinary or meningeal symptoms beyond those above.
- Travel and exposures:
  - Returned from Vietnam 4 weeks prior; rural and countryside exposure, trekking and cycling through farmland.
  - Reports having taken malaria prophylaxis while traveling but cannot recall the drug name; reports it was likely a daily regimen and also stated “another one that I took on top of the first one” (dose/route/frequency not documented; uncertainty noted).
- Past medical history:
  - Chronic back pain; currently under physiotherapy for posture-related back pain.
- Medications:
  - Seroxat (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Occasional over-the-counter paracetamol and ibuprofen taken at recommended doses (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies:
  - Pollen (hay fever). No drug allergies reported.
- Social / preventive care:
  - Occupation: nurse.
  - Up to date with vaccinations including hepatitis B.
  - Non-smoker. Moderate alcohol intake. Performs moderate exercise a few times per week.
- Family history:
  - Father deceased from myocardial infarction in his 60s (reported age ~68).

Examination:
- (No physical examination findings documented.)
- Vitals: not documented.

Impression:
- Febrile illness of unclear focus in a returning traveler. Differential includes malaria and other infectious causes; no obvious localizing symptoms identified on history.

Plan:
- Arrange in-person clinic assessment for physical examination to look for source of infection.
- Arrange blood tests after clinical review; specifically requested:
  - Thick and thin blood films to evaluate for malaria.
  - Inflammatory markers and other routine blood tests as clinically indicated (specific panels to be determined by examining clinician).
- Patient advised not to work until assessment and investigations are completed.
- Options for assessment:
  - Attend central London clinic for exam and testing (patient agreed to come in today).
  - Alternatively, attend local A&E if more convenient.
- Administrative steps:
  - Doctor will document suggested tests and instructions in the consultation notes for presentation at reception/A&E.
  - Admin team to contact patient to book clinic slot; patient to call the number left in the consultation notes to be slotted in.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation).
  - Physical examination findings.
  - Exact name, dose and regimen of malaria prophylaxis.
  - Exact dose/route/frequency of Seroxat and OTC analgesics.
  - Pregnancy status (not documented).
  - Specific laboratory results (none yet).
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Patient uncertain about malaria prophylaxis: cannot recall drug name; states it was likely daily and also said “another one that I took on top of the first one” — ambiguity/conflict noted regarding regimen.
- Transcript quality:
  - Overall adequate and intelligible for clinical documentation; occasional filler words and brief unclear phrases but majority of clinical information clear.
